full_judgment:
2. Opposite Party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted this 0. C. Suit No. 340 of 1980 which was subsequently renumbered as 0. C. Suit No. 148 of 1984 for reconveyance of the deed of the suit land under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It is alleged that on 6.5.1968 a deed of mort gage was executed to get the land back within 7 years. But as the present petitioner refused to reconvey the land he filed an application before the Circle Officer (Revenue) Charghat and the Circle Officer (Revenue) passed an order in favour of the plaintiff. There after an appeal was preferred before the Additional Deputy Commissioner 9 (Revenue) Rajshahi but the said proceeding was stayed. According to law the plaintiff is entitled to get the land back as the deed. of sale is on out sale with an agreement of reconveyance under sec-tion 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He prayed that a direction should be given to the defendant to register a deed giving back his land. 

 3. Defendants No. 1, 3 and 4 appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement stating that on 6.5.1968 and 6.8.1968 the plaintiff by two documents sold the suit lands to defendants No. 1 and the defendant No. 1 by a registered document transferred the aforesaid land to one Abdul Khaleque and others. Subsequently by a registered document dated 2.6.1978 Abdul Khaleque and other sold the suit land to defendants No. 3 and 4. 

 6. Mr. Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that in this case only two documents namely, Exts. 4 and 5 are matters for consideration. He submits that both the courts below misinterpreted, misconstrued and misunderstood these two documents. He submits that these two documents are not the deed of reconveyance for out and out sale. There is not a single word regarding reconveyance nor there is any separate agreement for reconveyance of the suit land. Only when section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force after independence of Bangladesh the plaintiff became encouraged of the aforesaid provision and filed the instant suit in the year 1980 but from the year 1968 this land travelled from one hand to another hand which is discussed above. During this long period from 1968 the plaintiff did not file any suit for such relief. I have personally considered each and every line of these two registered deeds of sale of the year 1968 and it appears to me that these two deeds are clearly and unequivocally the deeds of out and out and by no stretch of imagination it can be construed as deeds of out and out sale with an agreement of reconveyance. 

 7. Both the courts below relied on oral evidence and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. But the thing is that these two sale deeds being Exts. 4 and 5 are registered sale deeds of the, year 1968 when sec-tion 95A of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act was n()t born even. These two registered deeds of out and out sale without any condition shall prevail over other oral evidence and this cannot be construed in any manner whatsoever as an out and out sale with an agreement of reconveyance, So, the question of invoking section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act does not arise at all. Other evidence which were adduced before the court against these two registered documents cannot be accepted at all in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. So, I hold that both the courts below misinterpreted, misunderstood and misconstrued these two old registered sale deeds of the year 1968. As such, the judgment and decrees passed by both the courts below cannot be sustained under law. I hold that both the courts below committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice in decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff.
